display_name: Isle of Skye 21 Year Old (Blended Scotch, Ian Macleod)
cask: Blend of peated island malts matched with Speyside and Highland malts plus grain whiskies. Specific cask regime N/A — not found (TWW notes 'Chestnut/Oloroso sherry' colour only).
outturn_or_availability: Ongoing core-range expression; not limited. 70cl. SRP US$114.99.

tasting.nose: Warm baking spices, red apples, buttery toffee, citrus and chocolate malted balls; a beautiful dry nuttiness with brown sugar, vanilla, cedar chest, nutmeg, cinnamon, dried citrus, coffee and walnut cake.
tasting.palate: Subtle stone-fruit sweetness — spicy caramel, blackcurrant, chocolate, lemon zest, a hint of cedar wood and green peppercorn; sweet and honeyed with hot oatmeal, chocolate sauce, strawberries, orange and a whirl of ground pepper and oak spice.
tasting.finish: Medium to long, deliciously rich and oaky, with a glimpse of peppermint.
tasting.narrative: The entry into Skye's older blends, and it behaves like one: a 40% island blend that leads with confection — buttery toffee, red apple, chocolate malted balls and warm baking spice — over a spine of dry, savoury nuttiness (Whisky Advocate's McCormick logs brown sugar, cedar chest, coffee and walnut cake; The Whiskey Wash adds spicy caramel, blackcurrant and a hint of green peppercorn). The palate is sweet and honeyed, with oatmeal, chocolate sauce, strawberry and orange before a whirl of ground pepper, then a medium-to-long, deliciously rich and oaky finish closed by a glimpse of peppermint. Two decades show as polish, not depth — TWW concedes it lands 'without an over abundance of complexity' even as it calls it 'a subtly decadent treat'; Whisky Magazine's Chris Neil, scoring it 8.6, reads it as a 'beautiful, mature whisky' with dusty coffee, juicy barley and a long, stony finish. The hardware agrees the make is clean: Tastings.com/BTI awarded 90 points and a Gold. VERDICT: POUR. A genuinely well-made, smooth aged blend at a sane ~£118/$115 — buy it to drink, not to be moved; the 25 is where the money should go.
